title: AddDescribeData
description:
The describe a bare `add` of a git source returns: the source, what was discovered in it, and
exactly what would be written where — nothing has landed. `--yes` applies. **INFERRED**
(additive-only).

manifest.description: The manifest FILE the row would land in.

mcp.description:
The MCP SERVER this describe would import (`add --mcp <name|url>`): what the fetched
document says it is, where it points, and which agents would get it. Absent for every
other source — a git import has no endpoint to disclose. **INFERRED** (additive-only).

members.description: The skills discovered in it (leaf directory names).

note.description:
An honesty line the describe leads with when the manifest ALREADY spells this row (a
cloned file, a prior add whose installs failed): the row is demand, not consent — trust
in a forge origin is a store fact, so the describe still gates, and applying is what
fetches and installs the skills the row names. **INFERRED** (additive-only).

reference.description: The row key that would be written.

source.description: The source the add would take bytes from (e.g. `github.com/<owner>/<repo>`).

value.description: The row value that would be written (`"*"` or a commit pin).

McpServerSummary.description:
What a fetched MCP `server.json` says, after the gate accepted it — the facts a first-trust
describe puts in front of a person before any byte is written, and the facts the applied
receipt repeats. DERIVED from the document; the document itself is never echoed whole.
**INFERRED** (additive-only).

agents.description:
The agents detected here that the row would reach — the honest breadth line, so nobody
learns after the fact which config files were about to change.

auth.description:
The publisher's `_meta` auth word (`oauth` / `none`) when the document declared one.
Absent means it said nothing — which is NOT a claim that no credential is needed.

bundle.description: The folder the document would be written to (the bundle IS its directory).

description.description: The publisher's one-line summary (the registry caps it at 100 characters).

headers.description:
The names of the LITERAL headers every call will carry. A credential-shaped header never
reaches here — the gate refuses the whole document instead.

server.description: The registry name (`io.github.<owner>/<server>`) — the server's own identity.

transport.description:
The transport, always `streamable-http` today: the one a shared bundle can promise, since
the same URL has to work from every machine.

url.description: The endpoint an agent will call — always `https`, never a template.
